extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED staff, and USPTO regulatory counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements governing interim suspension of a practitioner from practice before the USPTO under 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.25, including service, deadlines, limited recognition, referral for formal discipline, and post-suspension obligations. Targets how and when suspension is imposed and what the respondent must (or may not) do during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for interim suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim suspension may be ordered when there is proof that the respondent committed a serious crime — e.g., a felony such as Online Solicitation of a Minor for Sexual Conduct (Tex. Penal Code § 33.021(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice/Order here states the request for interim suspension was predicated on proof that Respondent committed a serious crime; action taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.25 and 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Notice and Order (37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order must be sent by certified mail to the address provided by the respondent to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a) and to any address the OED Director reasonably believes the respondent receives mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order documents certified-mail service (lists receipt numbers) and notes the Notice and Order was delivered on a specific date; proper service starts statutory deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's response requirement — 40-day deadline (37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is directed to file, within forty (40) days, a response containing information sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact based upon any grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file a response within 40 days may permit the OED Director to determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and to enter interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination upon failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file the required response, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b) and conclude interim suspension and referral for formal proceedings are appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order notes Respondent's failure to file a response and so determines both lack of genuine issue and appropriateness of interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement and scope of interim suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim suspension from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO commences on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension applies to all practice before the Office (patent, trademark, other non-patent matters) effective immediately upon signing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of suspension — reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the Office until the OED Director grants a petition requesting the respondent's reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires compliance with the procedures and standards in § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office commencing on the date the Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after that date, solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrow, time-limited recognition is strictly for meeting obligations set out in § 11.58(b); it expires automatically after thirty days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (duties during suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (requirements imposed on a practitioner who has been suspended or disbarred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Order does not recite § 11.58's text, it mandates compliance (implied duties include notifying clients, transferring files, and taking steps to protect clients' interests as required by the regulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to hearing officer for formal disciplinary proceeding (37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint is referred to a hearing officer (here, at HUD Office of Hearings and Appeals) for the purpose of conducting a formal disciplinary proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral is made consistent with § 11.25(b)(5); the Order specifies the tribunal and the docket clerk contact information for filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer filing requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.36) — timeframe, addresses, PDP, and service
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty (30) days from the date of the Final Order, Respondent's written answer to the Complaint shall be filed with the designated hearing officer; a PDP version must be emailed to alj.alj@hud.gov; and a copy must be served on the OED Director at the specified address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides precise mailing and hand-delivery addresses (HUD OHA Docket Clerk) and requires electronic PDP submission and service to OED Director (Mail Stop 8, Office of the Solicitor, USPTO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Interim Suspension in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish in the Official Gazette a Notice of Interim Suspension stating the practitioner's name, registration number, the Interim Suspension action, and the felony/grounds (including statutory citation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order supplies a template Notice identifying the practitioner, registration number, offense (pled guilty to Online Solicitation of a Minor), and cites 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.25 and 11.59; disciplinary decisions are posted in OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to USPTO employees, federal agencies/courts, and state bar authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the Final Order to appropriate USPTO employees; to interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; and to appropriate authorities of any state in which the Respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This directs broad institutional notification to ensure other authorities and courts are informed of the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disassociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall disassociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational measure to prevent electronic practice/access tied to Customer Numbers and PKI during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for or being added to a USPTO Customer Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall his name be added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents circumvention of suspension by using or obtaining Customer Numbers until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of seeking review — no stay of suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent seeks a review of this suspension, any review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions for review/appeal do not automatically stay or delay the effective suspension order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing/Service address and procedural particulars for the formal proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific physical mailing and hand-delivery addresses for filing the answer with HUD OHA Docket Clerk are provided, and a PDP email address is specified for electronic filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order lists: Docket Clerk HUD OHA, 451 7th Street S.W., Room B-133, Washington DC 20410 (mail); 409 3rd Street S.W., Suite 201, Washington DC 20024 (hand-delivery); email alj.alj@hud.gov for PDP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public access to disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions regarding practitioners are posted at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's OED Reading Room electronically at the provided URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides where the public and interested parties can view disciplinary determinations (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).

rubrics_metrics.name: Catch-all authority for further relief
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order reserves 'such further relief as the nature of this cause shall require.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows the Office to impose additional measures as necessary consistent with the cause and regulations.
